014.title: I · Where it was found
014.line: A closing workshop on the outskirts of Kyoto.
014.after: The doors were shutting. The box was still on the bench.

014.title: II · How it was made
steps: The sap of the urushi tree.
Each left to cure before the next.

014.title: III · Untaught
014.words: Hand-lacquered using a technique its maker *never* *taught* to an apprentice.
014.after: There will be no second piece made this way.

014.title: V · As it was
014.note: The same object that sat on that workbench for forty years, now waiting on yours.

014.title: VI · The city behind it
014.line: Kyoto has worked lacquer for more than a thousand years.

014.title: VII · Yours
014.sub: 1 of 1. Once it's held, no one else can.

015.title: I · Where it was found
015.line: A family workshop in the Marrakech medina.

015.title: II · How it was made
015.line: Woven on a loom that will not be threaded again.
015.after: The weaver's hands have since moved to other work.

015.title: III · Where the pattern is kept
015.blurred: Not even fully in his memory of making it.

015.title: V · The city behind it
015.line: Weavers from the Atlas still bring their rugs down to the medina. Each pattern is carried in memory, not on paper.

015.title: VI · The record
015.note: Pulled from a family workshop, as it came off the loom.

015.title: VII · Yours
015.sub: 1 of 1. The pattern leaves with whoever holds it.

016.title: I · The kiln
016.line: Fired in a wood-burning kiln outside Oaxaca City.

016.title: III · How it came to us
lines: The potter does not usually keep a second of anything she makes.
She told us this was the piece she had planned to keep for herself.

016.title: V · The valleys behind it
016.after: Mercado Benito Juárez, steps from the zócalo, is where this craft still lives.

016.title: VI · The record
016.note: Not one of many. The one she had set aside.

016.title: VII · Yours
016.sub: 1 of 1. There was only ever one.

017.title: II · Who it was for
017.words: The fold above conforms to the *ear* *it* *was* *made* *for.*
017.after: A specific ear that the maker never named.

017.title: IV · The city behind it
017.after: The mines at Laurion paid for its fleet.

017.title: V · Where it still lives
017.line: Its jewellers still gather in the streets below the Acropolis.

017.title: VI · The record
017.note: There is no second pair. The form only works because it was made once.

017.title: VII · Yours
lines: Made for an ear the maker never named.
017.sub: 1 of 1. There is no second pair.

018.title: I · How it was carved
018.words: A block of limestone. Eyes *shut,* lips *parted,* cheekbones catching light from a direction the sculptor didn't predict.
018.after: A sheet of smoky glass rests above it, held by nothing visible.

018.title: IV · The city behind it
018.after: Portland stone fronts St Paul's and much of London rebuilt after the Great Fire.

018.title: V · The record
018.note: Carved limestone, smoked glass. The stone is the furniture.

018.title: VI · Yours
018.sub: 1 of 1. There is no second face.

003.title: Prologue · The wall
003.line: Lisbon's façades wear tile. One kitchen wears these.

003.title: I · Where it came from
003.line: Painted tile reached Lisbon five centuries ago and never left.
003.after: Whole façades of the city are still clad in azulejos.

003.title: III · The record
003.note: Once claimed, a listing does not return.

003.title: IV · Where it is now
lines: Re-laid into a kitchen wall outside Lisbon.
We were not told the address.

007.title: I · What it is
007.after: Jaipur's armourers made them for the Kachwaha court.

007.title: II · The city behind it
007.after: Laid out as a grid in 1727.

007.title: IV · The record
007.note: Once claimed, a listing does not return.

007.title: V · Where it is now
lines: Kept now in a drawer in Jaipur —

009.title: Prologue · The threshold
009.line: In Kerala the lamp is lit at the threshold, at dusk.

009.title: I · The metal
009.line: In Kerala, lamps are still cast by hand.

009.title: II · Where the craft still lives
009.line: Mannar has cast bell metal for generations.
009.after: Lamps and temple vessels are still cast there by hand.

009.title: IV · The record
009.note: Once claimed, a listing does not return.

009.title: V · Where it is now
lines: Lit once a year, somewhere in Kerala.
We were not invited to watch.

012.title: Prologue · The language
012.line: In the Andes, weaving is a language.

012.title: I · How it is learned
lines: Patterns passed from mother to daughter.
Spun from alpaca and sheep's wool.

012.title: II · How it is woven
012.line: Andean cloth is woven on a backstrap loom.
012.after: The weaver's own body holds the tension.

012.title: III · The city behind it
012.after: The Mercado de San Pedro, a few blocks from the Plaza de Armas, is where this craft still lives.

012.title: IV · The record
012.note: Once claimed, a listing does not return.

012.title: V · Where it is now
lines: waiting for an occasion that may not come.

019.title: II · The city behind it
019.line: Japanese blades are forged and folded in layers.
019.after: Patterned-steel kitchen knives carry that grain in every edge.

019.title: III · Where we are
019.last: We haven't found who folds it yet.

019.title: V · Not yet
lines: When we find who folds it,

020.title: I · How it was made
020.blurred: The furnace that made it has been cold for six years.

020.title: II · The city behind it
020.after: Murano's millefiori found a second home with makers in Perthshire and Caithness.

020.title: III · Where we are
lines: We know the colour exists somewhere on a shelf.
020.last: We haven't found the shelf yet.

020.title: V · Not yet
lines: a blue no one will mix again.

021.title: Prologue · The knot
021.line: A knot tied at a density no loom has matched.

021.title: I · How it is made
021.line: Dense enough that the back looks woven, not knotted.
021.after: No loom has matched it since the workshop closed.

021.title: II · Where we are
lines: We've traced two of these into private collections.
021.last: We're still looking for a third.

021.title: III · The city behind it
021.line: Once a working blanket on Nordic boats.
021.after: A long knotted pile to keep the cold out, before the rya moved to the wall.
